name: Qilin pills (Chinese herbal formula)
short: Few data. Trials in infertile men (12 weeks; alone, or with clomiphene): no obvious adverse events or reactions; one assessed blood, urine, liver and kidney tests, results not reported. No counts.
text: Few data; all from trials in men, and none of the abstracts lists the pills' herbs. In a multicentre randomized double-blind trial in 216 infertile men with low sperm count and motility, comparing Qilin pills with another Chinese formula (Wuziyanzong pills) for 12 weeks, safety was assessed with adverse events and blood and urine tests and liver and kidney function tests, and the conclusion states there were no obvious adverse events, but the abstract's results report no safety findings or counts. A multicentre open controlled trial of the same comparison (330 men) reaches the same conclusion without saying how adverse events were assessed. In a randomized trial in 300 men, Qilin pills added to clomiphene for 12 weeks showed no statistically significant difference in drug tolerance from clomiphene alone, and no obvious adverse reactions were observed. In a randomized trial in 63 men with late-onset hypogonadism, oral testosterone undecanoate plus Qilin pills had a lower rate of adverse reactions than testosterone alone, according to the conclusion; no figures are given. None of these abstracts reports an interaction with clomiphene or testosterone, and no other interaction data were found in the cited sources.
